facts.text: Putting the real sensor in the loop through HIL or over-the-air stimulation exercises the sensor's proprietary processing directly.

facts.text: Using a real sensor in the loop does not remove the need to validate the stimulation equipment itself.

facts.text: Using a real sensor in the loop does not remove the need to reproduce contamination and weather separately.

facts.text: Sensor sourcing contracts should include model-delivery and validation-data requirements now.

facts.text: Because the sensor type is still open, model-delivery and validation-data requirements can serve as a sensor selection criterion.

facts.text: When a supplier provides only object lists, validating a phenomenological sensor model at the same object-list interface is more defensible than inventing an unidentifiable raw-signal model.
